name: Connection Guard 0.6.2 candidate (PR #97, 3bdd753, zowi security)
relationship: Unreleased exact CI candidate for PR #97 acceptance against unchanged stable 0.6.1. Current master 29e6446 plus zowi security request. Does not contain later PR #101/#99. Not release qualification or a public product.

shipped.note: Unmodified new-install configuration, ENFORCE by default.

enforce.note: Single documented enforcement switch (config.yml comment and README: OBSERVE first, then ENFORCE).

proxycheck_key.note: enforce + the free ProxyCheck key through the product's documented key field (same key for every product).

free_keys.note: Adds the free ProxyCheck and VPNAPI keys through the product's documented key fields.

optimal.note: Best documented configuration (METHODOLOGY 4): failover order zowi, Blackbox (confirmed by Intel's hosting list), IPQuery; ProxyCheck off. In the providers runs of 7 and 13 Oct this caught 724 of 725 bad addresses and refused 2 of 616 clean ones; Blackbox before zowi refused none but caught 718 (99.0 vs 98.9 points, a tie). No free key improved it: every keyed service it supports (ProxyCheck, VPNAPI, IPHub) added refusals without catches. This is also the new-install order of PR #92.

documented_failure_policy: VPN OPEN; local Tor/Intel then zowi security mode, confirmed Blackbox and IPQuery. Existing quota, HTTP timeout and total lookup deadline unchanged.
telemetry: Connection Guard Cloud heartbeat to api.connectionguard.net (blocked at network level for every product's telemetry)
list_sources_note: Connection Guard Intel lists the shipped configuration downloads (relay.txt and hosting.txt never decide on their own). Intel is built from the same operator server lists as this dataset's VPN labels: its coverage here is circular (see the circularity table).
